case_name: Babu Ram and Another v State of Haryana and Another
respondent:
State of Haryana and Another
Supreme Court of India

7 October 2009
Civil Appeal No. 6864 of 2009 (Arising out of S.L.P. (C) No. 14302 of 2008)
The Judgment was delivered by : Altamas Kabir, J.

Act"), for construction of a Sewage Treatment Plant. petitioner_arguments: No urgency of such compelling nature had been disclosed by the respondents that warranted the invoking of Section 17(4) of the L.A. Act, 1894.

On the other hand, by denying the appellants the opportunity of filing objections under Section 5-A of the the L.A. Act, 1894, the respondents had tried to play down the fact that the STP was being constructed next to a school and grain market which would prove to be a health- hazard, not only for the students of the school, but for the inhabitants of the area in general.

In addition, Mr. Ghosh also submitted that in the plan which had been prepared by the Town Planning Department, it had been shown that the lands to be acquired were to be used for residential and commercial purposes and another plot had been earmarked for the Sewage Treatment Plant.
respondent_arguments: The Writ Court came to the conclusion that the provisions of Section 4 read with Section 17 had been religiously observed and followed by the Notification under Section 6, pursuant to which Award was announced on 23rd May, 2006.

In the said decision, this Court had pointed out that mere existence of an urgency or unforeseen emergency was not sufficient in itself to dispense with the provisions of Section 5-A of the aforesaid Act.
court_reasoning: The authority must have subjective satisfaction of the need for invoking urgency clause under Section 17 keeping in mind the nature of the public purpose, real urgency that the situation demands and the time factor i.e. whether taking possession of the property can wait for a minimum period within which the objections could be received from the landowners and the inquiry under Section 5-A of the Act could be completed.

Normally urgency to acquire a land for public purpose does not arise suddenly or overnight but sometimes such urgency may arise unexpectedly, exceptionally or extraordinarily depending on situations such as due to earthquake, flood or some specific time-bound project where the delay is likely to render the purpose nugatory or infructuous.
holding: The Special Leave Petition (now Civil Appeal) has been filed by the appellants questioning the dismissal of their writ petition.
The present acquisition proceeding was the second phase of acquisition of land purportedly for the purpose of setting up a Sewage Treatment Plant (STP).
